name: 报表与分析
description: The reporting read model: class overview, student report and student radar - three read-only routes over twelve tables owned by four other domains. Relocated from api/modules/insights (P4.3b.13), which is only possible because the owners published report ports first (P4.3b.12): classroom.public carries eight of the twelve tables including the four that belong to plugins/assignments, and engagement.public carries praises. This plugin owns no tables at all - data.adopted and data.reads are both empty - so it cannot drift into owning some.

data._adopted_note: Empty on purpose, and it is the point of the round. HANDOFF section 8.9 called this domain 'not a domain you can move on its own; it is a cross-domain read model' and deferred it until the owners had ports. It is also why `data.reads` is empty rather than listing the twelve tables: a read declaration here would let this plugin query them directly and re-derive what the ports already answer, which is exactly the 12-table implicit coupling section 8.9 warned about.
data._reads_note: Empty on purpose: every read goes through a port. classroom.public.getClassReportInputs / getStudentReportInputs / getStudentAccessView / countLeaveRequestsForStudents / listRecentLeaves cover students, classes, records, attendance_records, leave_requests, exams, student_exams, assignments and student_assignments; engagement.public covers praises. The four assignments-owned tables are the reason this round needed P4.3b.12 first: their class and student aggregates join `students`, which only classroom may do.
data._known_debt: 1. `engagement.public` is an OPTIONAL dependency resolved at call time, so a deployment with the engagement domain disabled renders reports with the praise half at zero (and logs a warning). That is the intended degradation, not a defect - a report must not be unreachable because a feature plugin is off. 2. The presentation arithmetic stays here rather than in the ports - `Math.round` of averages, the two rates with their zero guards, the radar's `min(100, ...)` and the 75/60 thresholds. The ports return raw numbers so exactly one place decides what a rate looks like; if a second consumer ever needs a rate, that is the moment to reconsider, not before. 3. `getClassReportInputs` deliberately does not carry the leave count: it would widen the class report for one integer, and the count needs the roster this plugin already resolves. Both choices are recorded so a later round can revisit them deliberately.
data._auth_note: All three routes resolve the caller with `requireActor` before any port call: 401 for anonymous (未登录或登录已过期), 403 for a known caller outside the matrix's scope (无权限访问该报告 / 无权限查看该班级分析). The static audit already saw an actor lookup in these handlers, but only the student-scoped access check refused an anonymous caller: `GET /api/analytics/classes/:classId/overview` answered 200 to anyone and skipped the check entirely for non-teachers. It now enforces `admin 任意；teacher 本班；parent 孩子；student 本人`, resolving a student's class or a parent's children through classroom.public when the host supplied no scope.
